subject: Triton Health — performance checklist & next steps
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@tritonhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Triton Health — performance checklist & next steps

Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written summary so we have the targets and next steps captured. Please correct anything I missed.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- High tail latency during peak 10:00–14:00 ET windows; several user-facing timeouts at p95.
- Current provider-level batching is causing jitter for streaming responses (partial token arrival not reliable).
- Cost/throughput tradeoffs causing engineering to run smaller models but hit quality regressions.

Current stack (what you told us):
- Frontend: Web chat + mobile app (long-lived streaming sessions).
- Backend: Internal inference proxy -> managed GPU endpoints (vendor X) -> Redis for short-term KV cache.
- Average concurrent live sessions: 650; expected seasonal peak ~1,200.
- Typical turn length: 30–120 tokens; occasional long generation up to ~1,000 tokens.

Success criteria you highlighted:
- P95 generation latency (end-to-end) <= 350 ms for short responses (<150 tokens), maintainable at 1k concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming UX: partial tokens must arrive within 100ms of model emit to avoid perceptible stalls.
- Cost: improve per-session token cost by >=20% or demonstrate an equivalent reliability benefit.
- Operational: rollout with canary and automatic fallback to smaller model under saturation.

Initial ideas / what Redwood would deliver:
- Dedicated routing to model variants (fast small model for short responses, fallback to higher-quality model when needed).
- Prefix and KV caching to reduce repeated context compute for frequent prompts.
- Streaming pipeline adjustments to prioritize low-latency partial-token delivery.
- Concurrency plan: baseline 1,500 concurrent streaming slots with autoscale headroom.

Attachments sent: RWI-quickstart.pdf (2-page quickstart), triton-midterm-slos.xlsx (template for defining SLOs), SLA-draft-Redwood.docx (starter SLA language).

Next steps (agreed):
1) Redwood: send a tailored SLO worksheet (attached) + a short checklist for streaming tuning — target by EOD today (Vivek).
2) Triton: share a sampled trace + a p95/p99 CSV for the busiest Thursday window (Alex / engineering) — target EOD Thu.
3) Ops & procurement: Alex to introduce Sara Johnson (procurement) for preliminary commercial questions and basic security docs.
4) Schedule a short proof-of-concept kickoff call (30 min) to scope a week-long perf pilot — propose Wed/Thu next week.

If that all looks right I can schedule the kickoff and include Marissa (solutions) and Hannah (reliability).

Thanks,
Vivek
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RWI-quickstart.pdf]
[Attachment: triton-midterm-slos.xlsx]

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@tritonhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:48:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Triton Health — performance checklist & next steps

Vivek — this is perfect, thanks for pulling together. A couple small clarifications: 
- Our measured p95 currently sits ~420 ms for short responses during peak (agrees with what I said). The p99 spikes can be 1.2–2s depending on model warmups.
- Concurrency planning: 1,200 is our conservative peak estimate; we often see short bursts to 1,600 for promo-driven traffic.

I copied Sara Johnson (procurement) on this thread — Sara, we expect to need a basic commercial/term ping + SOC2 evidence to move the pilot forward.

We will upload a 1-hour trace and the p95/p99 CSV to the Drive link you shared; engineering will flag any sensitive fields.

For the kickoff window Wed/Thu next week, Wed 10:00–10:30 ET works best for our engineers. Can your team make that?

Alex
Director of Product — Triton Health
[Inline: +1 (415) 555-0199]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Alex / Sara — great, Wed 10:00 ET works for our engineers. I've sent a calendar invite for Wed 2026-09-28 10:00–10:30 ET and included a short agenda: 1) Review trace & p95 targets, 2) scope pilot (data, duration, success metrics), 3) next steps for procurement.

Sara — welcome. To help procurement triage: I'll attach the SOC2 summary and a link to our standard pilot MSA; Marissa will follow up with the commercial points. If you prefer, we can do a separate procurement intro call after kickoff.

Immediate deliverables timeline (updated):
- Today EOD: Redwood sends tuned SLO worksheet + short streaming checklist (Vivek).
- Thu EOD: Triton uploads trace + p95/p99 CSV to Drive (Alex).
- Wed 2026-09-28 10:00 ET: Pilot kickoff (all).

HubSpot record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/company/67890 (I linked notes & next steps).

Thanks — looking forward to getting the pilot started.

Vivek
